newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania private bank says safe despite withdrawals.
newsitem.headline: Romania private bank says safe despite withdrawals.

text.p: Romania's private bank Bankcoop said on Wednesday it could honour withdrawals by individuals who started to queue at its branches following a row between the bank and its main shareholder this week.
"We don't have liquidity problems. The dispute has only a psychological effect on our depositors," said Banca de Credit Cooperatist Bankcoop SA spokesman Auras Albu.

People started on Monday to queue to withdraw their money from Bankcoop's major branches across Romania after the bank's president accused its major shareholder, prominent local businessman George Paunescu, of seeking to take control.
"I withdraw my savings because of rumours. We already had unhappy experiences with two other banks," said a man queueing at one of Bankcoop's Bucharest units.

Over the past year problems at two private banks -- Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA and Dacia Felix SA -- undermined confidence in the banking sector, which is still dominated by state-owned banks.
When Dacia Felix and Credit Bank troubles emerged publicly depositors in the two banks rushed to collect their savings.
"From now on I'll keep my money under the mattress," said a pensioner queueing at a Bankcoop branch in Timisoara, on the western border with Yugoslavia and Hungary.
But Bankcoop's Albu said the panic would fizzle out: "We have 300 billion lei in liquidities, things are under control."
In an impromptu news conference late on Sunday, Bankcoop president Alexandru Dinulescu said Paunescu, who holds 44 percent of Bankcoop's capital, was seeking to take control.
Paunescu on Monday rejected the claim saying they were "an attempt to cover bad management at the bank".
In separate statements on Wednesday, both men urged clients to keep their faith in the bank, which they said was solid.
Dinulescu asked the central bank to launch an inquiry into Paunescu's aquisition of Banckoop shares.
Central bank officials said they had started checks at Bankcoop but gave no further details.

In 1995 Bankcoop fought off local market and media speculation alleging problems at the bank. Later that year Paunescu, head of a large media and tourism holding and an influential figure on Romania's emerging markets, acquired $10 million worth of Bankcoop shares.

The row with Paunescu came in the wake of Bankcoop's report of an end-1996 provisional balance sheet of 2.1 trillion lei ($465 million), 870 billion lei up from 1995 and a 1996 gross profit of 66 billion ($14.6 million).
